stream(name, continuationToken=None, nextStepSeqNum=None, snapshot=None, x__xgafv=None) 
Read-only server-stream of a task's execution by id: trajectory steps and status changes, resumable from a step sequence number. Unlike CreateTaskBidiStream, it does not accept client inputs -- use it to observe or replay a task (the trajectory is not stored on the Task resource). This is the entry point for *observers*: it tails the trajectory from interaction storage without restoring the runtime actor, so it adds no restore latency and continues to follow output that a participant driving the task on a CreateTaskBidiStream connection produces. Observe-only clients should prefer this over a subscribe_task connect on CreateTaskBidiStream, which restores the actor and is meant for clients that will send input.

Args:
  name: string, Required. The name of the task to stream. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} (required)
  continuationToken: string, Optional. Opaque resume cursor, as issued on TaskServerEvent.continuation_token. Replay continues immediately after the event that carried the token. Takes precedence over next_step_seq_num when both are set. A token this stream cannot redeem is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than silently falling back to the numeric cursor, so a client cannot mistake a rejected resume for a replay from the start; reconnect without a token instead. That covers a malformed token, one issued by a connection whose delta streaming differs from this one's (see TaskSpec.delta_streaming), one issued while the server derived task status differently, and any token on a recurring task. A token names a position in the task it was issued on; send it only to that task. It carries no task id, so a token from another task is not rejected, and what it returns is undefined. A token whose position is past the events stored so far is not an error either, because storage can trail the live stream that issued the token: the replay skips everything up to that position, so a snapshot may return no events.
  nextStepSeqNum: string, Optional. The next step sequence number to resume from. When zero, streams from the beginning of the available trajectory.
  snapshot: boolean, Optional. If true, streams only the events produced up to the current point in time and terminates the stream once all existing events are sent, rather than tailing and waiting for future events.
  x__xgafv: string, V1 error format.
    Allowed values
      1 - v1 error format
      2 - v2 error format

Returns:
  An object of the form:

    { # Server -> Client message for TaskService.CreateTaskBidiStream. * The first message carries a connect_reply (task_created or task_subscribed). * The steady-state pattern is repeated `events` (steps, status). * The last message carries an end_signal.
  "ackInputSeqNum": "A String", # Optional. When non-zero, confirms cumulative receipt of client input through this seq_num (inclusive).
  "assignedAgentIdentity": "A String", # Output only. The resolved Agent Identity (SPIFFE ID) of the `Agent` this task is assigned to. Populated on the first message of the stream.
  "events": [ # Steady-state events from the server (trajectory steps -- including elicitation/tool-call HITL requests -- and status changes).
    { # A single Server -> Client event. There is intentionally no non-terminal error/notice branch. Transient, retriable failures (tool-fetch retry, rate-limit, scheduler retry) are handled by runtime retry (bounded by TaskSpec.max_retries) and, if surfaced at all, appear as trajectory steps; the terminal error is reported once via TaskCompletedEvent.outcome.status (google.rpc.Status). This follows the Interactions events.proto, which deprecated its dedicated non-terminal InteractionPausedEvent and reports terminal status on InteractionCompletedEvent.
      "continuationToken": "A String", # Optional. Opaque resume cursor covering everything delivered through this event, inclusive. A client that keeps the token from the last event it processed and passes it back on SubscribeTaskEvent.continuation_token or StreamTaskRequest.continuation_token resumes at the next event, with no gap and no duplicate. Opaque: the encoding is a server implementation detail and may change without notice. Do not parse it, compare two of them, or derive ordering from it -- order by `seq_num`. Carries no task id, because every RPC that redeems a token already names the task it applies to. It is a position, not a capability: it grants no access on its own, and the task's IAM check is what authorizes the read. This is the resume cursor. Resuming by number (next_step_seq_num on SubscribeTaskEvent and StreamTaskRequest) is slated for deprecation: a number cannot address a position inside a streamed step, while the token can, so a reconnect mid-answer does not re-send the part of that answer the client already rendered. `seq_num` remains for ordering only.
      "eventId": "A String", # Optional. The TaskClientEvent.event_id this event was derived from, echoed back verbatim. Set only on the events that carry a client input back out: the `step` echoing the input, and the `step_start` of a streamed step the input opened. Empty everywhere else -- on model-generated steps the server produced on its own, on the step_delta/step_stop frames continuing a run (correlate those by `index` with their step_start), and on any event whose client input carried no event_id. Purely a correlation handle: it does not order or acknowledge anything, and the server never derives behavior from it. Since the server does not enforce uniqueness, a client that reuses an id sees it on every echo it produced. Delivered to every client subscribed to the task, not just the one that sent the input, including on a later replay from storage.
      "seqNum": "A String", # Required. 1-based, non-decreasing sequence number within the server direction, stable across reconnects, so it can be used to resume: a given event carries the same number however the stream is (re)connected. Gapless on a stream delivered from the beginning. Clients acknowledge receipt via ack_output_seq_num and resume via SubscribeTaskEvent.next_step_seq_num. A resume with next_step_seq_num = 0 (or unset) restarts from the first still available step. A number identifies a resume point, not an event, so it is not unique: consecutive events can share one. An event derived from another (an artifacts_changed delta carrying the plan its step just wrote) repeats its source's number rather than taking the next, which keeps the numbering a function of the stream alone and guarantees a cursor never lands between the two. Acknowledging a number acknowledges every event carrying it. A resume can begin AFTER the requested number. next_step_seq_num counts events, but a streamed step spans several of them, so a cursor can point inside a run; the server then suppresses that run's remaining step_delta/step_stop rather than deliver frames for a step the client never saw opened, and resumes at the next step boundary. Numbering is unchanged by that suppression -- keeping it stable is what makes a cursor meaningful across connections -- so the first delivered event may be a later number than asked for. Treat the sequence as monotonic, not densely contiguous, when resuming.

suspend(name, body=None, x__xgafv=None) 
Suspends a task, pausing its active turn or scheduling loop and transitioning the status to SUSPENDED. The underlying runtime session remains resumable.

Args:
  name: string, Required. The name of the task to suspend. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} (required)
  body: object, The request body.
    The object takes the form of:

{ # Request for TaskService.SuspendTask.
  "operateOnSelf": True or False, # Optional. Whether to skip cascade suspension to all descendant subtasks. Defaults to false (cascades to all descendants by default).
  "statusDetail": { # Why a task is in its current status, when the status alone is not enough to act on (today: `SUSPENDED`). Clients MUST treat an unrecognized `StatusReason` as an opaque block. Copied to the DB mirror by name and number, so a field or enum value added here without the matching DB-side addition is silently dropped on write. LINT.IfChange(status_detail) # Optional. Machine-readable reason and detail for the suspension.
    "detail": "A String", # Optional human-readable explanation, so a surface can render something without its own StatusReason -> string table. upload(name, body=None, media_body=None, media_mime_type=None, x__xgafv=None) 
Uploads a file. The file is sent as media: post it to this method's URL with an `/upload` prefix, e.g. `/upload/v1beta1/{name}:upload`, carrying `path` as request metadata and the file's bytes as the media content. The task must not be in a terminal state, and an existing file at `path` is replaced. At most 10 GiB.

Args:
  name: string, Required. The task or collaborative project to upload to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project} (required)
  body: object, The request body.
    The object takes the form of:

{ # Request for ArtifactService.UploadArtifact.
  "path": "A String", # Required. Absolute destination path in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.md`. Must be under `/workspace` and at most 1024 characters; relative paths and paths containing a `..` segment are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
}

  media_body: string, The filename of the media request body, or an instance of a MediaUpload object.
  media_mime_type: string, The MIME type of the media request body, or an instance of a MediaUpload object.
  x__xgafv: string, V1 error format.
    Allowed values
      1 - v1 error format
      2 - v2 error format

Returns:
  An object of the form:

    { # Response for ArtifactService.UploadArtifact.
  "path": "A String", # The file's path in the task's workspace.
}
uploadArtifact(task, body=None, path=None, x__xgafv=None) 
Uploads a file into a task's workspace. A client-streaming RPC: the request body is the file's raw bytes, relayed to storage a chunk at a time, so neither ESF nor this server holds the whole file. A broken connection restarts the upload from zero. `path` must be an absolute path under `/workspace/userdata/`. The task must not be in a terminal state. An existing file at `path` is replaced. At most 1 GiB.

  task: string, Required. The task to upload into. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} (required)
  body: object, The request body.
